source.title: An essay on some problems of approximation theory

accepted.question_text: Let f be an unknown smooth T-periodic real-valued function on R. Suppose an approximate datum f_delta in L^infty(R) is known, with ||f_delta - f||_infty < delta, and suppose the derivative of f is uniformly bounded by m1 < infinity. Can the derivative of f be approximated stably in the L^infty(R) norm using only the data {delta, f_delta, m1}, in the sense that the approximation error tends to 0 as delta tends to 0?

evidence.quote: Can one approximate stably in L∞(R) the derivative f′

accepted.question_text: Let D be a bounded domain in R^n with n >= 3. For m = 1,2, let L_m be a formal linear partial differential operator and let N(L_m) = {w : L_m w = 0 in D} be its null-space in D. Can every function f in L^2(D), or more generally in L^p(D) for p >= 1, be approximated with arbitrary accuracy by finite linear combinations of products u_1 u_2, where u_m belongs to N(L_m) and the products are well defined?
accepted.context_brief: Property C and products of PDE solutions

evidence.quote: can one approximate, with an arbitrary accuracy

accepted.question_text: Let f be supported in a bounded set D in R^n, and let its Fourier transform be known only on a domain D_tilde in frequency space. Can f be recovered from the values of its Fourier transform on D_tilde, and can one give an analytic inversion formula for recovering f, equivalently for spectrally extrapolating the Fourier transform of a compactly supported function from partial frequency-domain data?

evidence.quote: can one recover f(x) from the knowledge
